LESSON: RUGBY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.5: Rugby

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Rugby. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are the best ways to advance a ball in a game of Rugby?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. perform passing skills in Rugby
2. perform kick techniques in Rugby
3. value own and others' efforts in applying passing and kicking skills for enjoyment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: RUGBY
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Rugby helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: RUGBY
Study Rugby like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Perform passing skills in Rugby

What this means
In this part you learn to perform passing skills in Rugby. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform passing skills in Rugby.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Rugby” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform passing skills in Rugby. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Perform kick techniques in Rugby

What this means
In this part you learn to perform kick techniques in Rugby. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform kick techniques in Rugby.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Rugby in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform kick techniques in Rugby. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Value own and others' efforts in applying passing and kicking skills for enjoyment

What this means
In this part you learn to value own and others' efforts in applying passing and kicking skills for enjoyment. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value own and others' efforts in applying passing and kicking skills for enjoyment.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value own and others' efforts in applying passing and kicking skills for enjoyment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Rugby is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Rugby” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: perform passing skills in Rugby)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Rugby in your own words. (skill: perform kick techniques in Rugby)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: value own and others' efforts in applying passing and kicking skills for enjoyment)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Rugby to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: perform passing skills in Rugby.
3. Practise this skill: perform kick techniques in Rugby.
4. Practise this skill: value own and others' efforts in applying passing and kicking skills for enjoyment.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Rugby from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Rugby: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Rugby?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the best ways to advance a ball in a game of Rugby?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Rugby means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: perform passing skills in Rugby.
5. Be able to: perform kick techniques in Rugby.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
